facts.statement: Oligocolius lived during the Early to Late Oligocene epoch.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early–Late Oligocene

facts.statement: The genus Oligocolius was described by the authority Mayr in the year 2000.
facts.quote: authority: Mayr, 2000

facts.statement: The first specimen was found in a clay pit at Frauenweiler near Wiesloch, Germany, dating to approximately 32 million years ago.
facts.quote: The first specimen of Oligocolius was discovered in a clay pit at Frauenweiler, near Wiesloch in Germany, dated to the Rupelian approximately 32 million years ago during the early Oligocene

facts.statement: Palaeontologist Gerald Mayr described and named the species in 2000.
facts.quote: The specimen was described and named by palaeontologist Gerald Mayr in 2000

facts.statement: A second specimen was described by Mayr in 2013 from the 24.7 million-year-old Enspel lagerstätte.
facts.quote: A second specimen was later described by Mayr in 2013 from the late Oligocene (24.7 Ma) lagerstätte in Enspel

facts.statement: Oligocolius is an extinct genus of mousebird from the Oligocene epoch of Germany.
facts.quote: Oligocolius (meaning "Oligocene mousebird") is an unusual genus of extinct mousebird from the early to late Oligocene epoch of Germany

facts.statement: Oligocolius belongs to the family Coliidae and is broadly similar in shape to modern mousebirds.
facts.quote: Oligocolius is a member of the family of modern mousebirds (Coliidae) and is broadly similar to them in shape

facts.statement: Unlike modern mousebirds, the skull and beak of Oligocolius closely resemble those of parrots.
facts.quote: However, unlike modern mouse birds the skull and beak of Oligocolius closely resembles those of parrots

facts.statement: The skull of Oligocolius is remarkably parrot-like due to its broad intertemporal region and beak shape.
facts.quote: The skull of Oligocolius is remarkably parrot-like, particularly due to the broad intertemporal region between the eyes and the shape of the beak

facts.statement: The upper beak of Oligocolius was deep, rounded, and possibly hooked at the tip, unlike the short beaks of modern mousebirds.
facts.quote: The upper beak is deep and rounded, as well as possibly hooked at the tip, compared to the short finch-like beaks of modern mousebirds

facts.statement: Oligocolius had a particularly long retroarticular process on its mandible where jaw-opening muscles attach.
facts.quote: The mandible has a particularly long retroarticular process, where the muscle for opening the jaws attaches to at the back of the lower jaw

facts.statement: The upper beak of Oligocolius was freely mobile due to a hinge between the nasal bones and frontals, similar to parrots and toucans.
facts.quote: the beak is attached to the cranium by a hinge between the nasal bones and the frontals, meaning the upper beak was freely mobile like those of parrots and toucans

facts.statement: The tarsometatarsus of Oligocolius was much shorter than its humerus and ulna, unlike any other known coliiform.
facts.quote: The tarsometatarsus of the foot is much shorter than in any other known coliiform, much shorter than the humerus and ulna

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows O. psittacocephalon contained many fruit stones inside its body, mostly clustered beneath the skull.
facts.quote: O. psittacocephalon was found with many fruit stones inside its body, mostly in a cluster beneath the skull and a few within the body cavity

facts.statement: The fruit stones found in O. psittacocephalon were about 0.5 mm in size and completely intact.
facts.quote: The size of the stones are about as large as the biggest fruits swallowed by living mousebirds (0.5 mm) and are completely intact

facts.statement: Evidence indicates Oligocolius consumed larger fruits than living mousebirds and swallowed them whole.
facts.quote: indicating that Oligocolius not only consumed larger fruits than living mousebirds but that it also swallowed them whole

facts.statement: The presence of a crop implies Oligocolius fed on tougher fruits and vegetation than living mousebirds.
facts.quote: The presence of a crop in Oligocolius implies that it was feeding on fruits and vegetation that was tougher to digest than those in the diet of living mousebirds

facts.statement: Researchers infer that the crop evolved independently in Oligocolius since it is absent in living mousebirds and their close relatives.
facts.quote: Because the crop is absent in living mousebirds, and that mousebirds are not closely related to other birds with crops (such as the hoatzin and raptors), it is inferred that the crop was evolved independently in at least Oligocolius amongst mousebirds

facts.statement: Longer, stronger wings allowed Oligocolius to fly longer distances than living mousebirds.
facts.quote: The longer and more strongly developed wings of Oligocolius would have allowed it to fly for longer distances than living mousebirds

facts.statement: Oligocolius likely spent more time in trees and dispersed more easily than other coliids.
facts.quote: Oligocolius likely spent more time in the trees than living mousebirds, and was capable of dispersing more easily than other coliids

facts.statement: It is uncertain if Oligocolius's adaptations were a response to a cooling climate in Europe between the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum and the Miocene Climatic Optimum.
facts.quote: It's possible that unusual adaptations of Oligocolius were a response to a period of cooling climate in Europe between the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum and the Miocene Climatic Optimum, although this is uncertain

facts.statement: Oligocolius is the only known coliid from the Oligocene epoch.
facts.quote: Oligocolius is the only coliid known from the Oligocene

facts.statement: The parent group of Oligocolius is the family Coliidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coliidae

facts.statement: The time range for Oligocolius is from the Rupelian to the Chattian stages, between 33.9 and 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Chattian (33.9 to 23.04 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Oligocolius was similar in size to living mousebirds like the speckled mousebird.
rejected.quote: Oligocolius was similar in size to living mousebirds (such as the speckled mousebird) with a superficially similar shape

rejected.quote: In addition to the parrot-like skull, Oligocolius also has notably shorter feet and longer wings than modern mousebirds
